newsitem.title: GERMANY: 20 to list on Germany's New Market in first year.
newsitem.headline: 20 to list on Germany's New Market in first year.

text.p: Twenty companies are still expected to list on Germany's fledgling "New Market" for growth stocks in its first year, although only two have listed so far, German bourse operator Deutsche Boerse AG said on Tuesday.

New Market, modelled on New York's NASDAQ exchange, had got off to a "fulsome start" in terms of share prices and liquidity since its March 10 launch, Deutsche Boerse board member Reto Francioni told the group's annual news conference.

Thus far only mobile telephone services firm MobilCom and engineering services group Bertrandt have opted to list on the New Market, which is mainly aimed at innovation stocks, but Francioni said more are coming soon.

"We will see announcements from a number of companies planning to list on the New Market segment in coming weeks," Francioni said, but the next flotation would only take place in three or four months.
Francioni would not be drawn on the names of companies planning to list or say what sectors they come from.
New Market was set up in March amid hopes that it would breathe new life into Germany's cautious investment world.

It was developed and is promoted by Deutsche Boerse and is designed to encourage innovative young firms to tap into a small but growing demand in Germany for potentially high-yielding, risk-bearing investments.
Analysts are sceptical about the initiative, Frankfurt's latest bid to overcome a reputation for a lack of innovation and gain an edge over international rivals.
Aimed mainly at high-technology businesses, New Market offers firms advice and publicity on public offerings and a guarantee of liquidity after their stock starts trading.
In return, companies must meet strict entry requirements on issue conditions and transparency to reduce risks, including publishing quarterly results and using International Accounting Standards.
